audit_notes: Parameters positive and within bounds. Lid flexural rigidity D = E t^3/(12(1-nu^2)) = 1.37e-11 N m; clamped strip under the pulse pressure: w_max = p a^4/(384 D) = 4.75 um (0.95 t, edge of linear plate theory; membrane stiffening lowers real strain by ~15-30 %). Peak edge strain eps = 16 t w_max/a^2 = 0.152, the same as the mm-scale parent because p a^2/(E t^2) is kept constant; this exceeds the 0.10 biofilm detachment strain. Swept volume per pulse = a * (8/15) w_max per unit length = 1.27e-10 m2, i.e. a film of 2.1 um per pulse at 60 um pitch; the lubricant pumping part is physically sound. Caveats that limit the claimed drag benefit: (1) an expelled open film of 2 um is sheared downstream within seconds at 50 Pa wall shear (film speed tau h/mu_o ~ 0.2 m/s), so the lubricant slip is transient and only the fouling-shedding part gives a lasting benefit unless the film is retained in texture; (2) a 5 um elastomer lid is far thinner than any hull coating that survives abrasion, fenders, cleaning brushes or cavitation - durability over several years is the decisive open point, not the mechanics of one pulse; (3) the pressure line must be referenced to ambient hydrostatic pressure; (4) the pore must act as a valve (closes when the lid is flat) or seawater and bacteria enter the reservoir. The solved field is lid deflection; the drag effect (avoided slime penalty ~10-15 % plus transient slip) cannot be computed from it, and a static, non-pulsed lid has zero strain, so no meaningful relative baseline exists: baseline left empty, gain reported as n/a.
